before.stem: ww A 40 year old female presents to ED complaining of complete visual loss in her right eye. On fundoscopy you note a pale retina and a cherry red spot. You suspect an emboli. Which of the following blood vessels is most likely the source of the emboli:
options: Anterior cerebral artery (x) Middl cerebral artery 8%
Posterior cerebral artery (Vv) Internal carotid artery 56%
warnings: No marked correct option was detected.
before.explanation: The internal carotid artery is the most likely source of the emboli. The ophthalmic artery arises from the internal carotid artery and supplies structures in the orbit and eyeball. The central retinal artery is the most important branch of the ophthalmic artery, supplying the retina and the optic disc. The central retinal artery is an end artery that does not anastomose with other arteries, and thus its occlusion results in monocular blindness. : Vv
